newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares creep higher in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares creep higher in dull trade.

text.p: Lithuanian stocks crept up slightly in trade that was fairly light on Tuesday although dealers said that there was room for more upward momentum.

The group A index rose 24.79 points to 2,410.72 on trade of 1.06 million litas. Dealers said prices should rise in the short-term but do not expect a repeat of the bull run that sent prices to new highs in January.

"We are now seeing a price adjustment process. Prices seem to have bottomed out and we expect them to rise five to 10 percent over the next few weeks," Suprema brokerage dealer Tomas Andrejauskas said.
Gainers included Hermis Bank, which rose two percent to 204 litas on trade of 56,100 litas.
The bank said earlier that its 1996 profit was expected to be 25 million litas, sharply higher than the 3.6 million litas of 1995.
"That forecast is in line with what the market expects and if it holds it will certainly help to boost Hermis' share price," one dealer said.
Among the losers was Kalnapilis brewery, which fell to 7.18 litas from 7.97 litas. Demand for debt was also low and there were no deals on the secondary T-bill market.
